comments.text:
If I want the specific color grading control that lightroom has I can point it there and I'll get the exact math. I did reverse engineering manually before and it's tedious to say the least, I'd normally much rather wing the color math than clone it. Winging something can take some experimentation iterations and doesn't guarantee a good result either.

That said, REA is quite poorly designed and I hope someone with a bit more agentic experience will create something proper. And I will not install and use gigantic 1:1 clones made by random people over the weekend, offering no support and holding no responsibility. Not defending adobe here cause they're evil, but I have standards. Cool party trick though.

comments.text: REA uses actual decompilers to read code instructions, that's why it takes longer but also produces better results, if you vibe it the model is just guessing, using REA it reads actual instructions, passes it to a tester and compares, if the results are not the same it decompiles again until it gets it exact, so you can recreate features faithfully with enough time. it's most impactful in things like device emulation, where exactness is a must, if you're just copying a feature then yeah, it doesn't have to be exact byte for byte like you would get from REA
